operations.description:
This endpoint enables prospective users to create new accounts for the Todo application. Users provide their email address and desired password through a registration form. The system validates that the email follows RFC 5322 standard email format and is not already registered in the system. The password is validated to meet minimum security requirements (8+ characters). Upon successful validation, the system creates a new user record in the todo_app_users table with status set to 'active', automatically hashes the password using bcrypt before storage (never stored in plaintext), and records the creation timestamp (created_at) in UTC timezone.

Upon successful registration, the system generates and issues a JWT access token (expires in 30 minutes) and a refresh token (expires in 7 days) containing the user's ID, email, and 'user' role claim. The user is automatically authenticated and logged in immediately after registration without requiring a separate login step. The registered user immediately gains access to create, view, update, and delete their own todo items.

If the email address is already registered in the system, the operation fails with error code AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS and message 'An account with this email already exists. Please log in or use a different email.' If the password is shorter than 8 characters, the operation fails with error code AUTH_WEAK_PASSWORD and message 'Password must be at least 8 characters long.' If email format is invalid, the operation fails with error code AUTH_INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT.

This registration operation is public and does not require prior authentication. All user accounts are created with 'active' status and immediately usable. The operation creates corresponding empty user sessions and initializes user preferences during account creation. Related operations include login (/auth/user/login) for existing users and password reset (/auth/user/password/reset) for account recovery.

operations.specification: User account login endpoint enabling users to authenticate with email and password credentials. This operation validates user credentials against stored password hash in todo_app_users table, verifies account is in 'active' status, creates a user session record in todo_app_user_sessions table with connection metadata (IP address, referrer, connection URL), generates JWT access and refresh tokens, and returns authentication response with user information and tokens. The endpoint implements security measures including lockout after failed attempts, constant-time password comparison, and session tracking.

operations.description:
This endpoint enables registered users to authenticate and establish an active session. Users provide their registered email address and password. The system verifies the email exists in the todo_app_users table and retrieves the associated password hash. The system validates the provided password against the stored hash using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks, ensuring secure password verification without revealing password hints to attackers.

Upon successful authentication, the system verifies the user's account status is 'active' (not 'inactive' or 'deleted'). If account status is not 'active', authentication is denied with appropriate error message. The system then creates a new session record in the todo_app_user_sessions table, capturing the session metadata including IP address (from request), HTTP referrer, and connection URL for security auditing and tracking login locations.

The system generates JWT access token (valid 30 minutes) and refresh token (valid 7 days) containing user ID, email, and 'user' role claim. Access token is used for subsequent authenticated API requests. Refresh token enables obtaining new access tokens without re-entering credentials. The response includes user information (ID, email, status), both tokens with their expiration times, and confirmation of successful authentication.

Multiple concurrent sessions are supported - users can log in from different devices simultaneously. If the email address is not found in the system, authentication fails with error code AUTH_USER_NOT_FOUND and generic message 'We couldn't find an account with that email address.' If the password is incorrect, authentication fails with error code AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS and generic message 'Your password is incorrect. Please try again.' After 5 consecutive failed login attempts within 15 minutes, the account is temporarily locked for 30 minutes with error code AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED.

This operation is public and does not require prior authentication. Failed login attempts are logged for security monitoring. Successful logins update the user's activity timestamp. Related operations include registration (/auth/user/join), token refresh (/auth/user/refresh), and password reset (/auth/user/password/reset) for account recovery.

This operation validates the refresh token, verifies it has not expired and belongs to an active user account, generates and returns a new access token (30-minute expiration) and optionally issues a new refresh token (7-day expiration). The refresh token remains valid in todo_app_user_sessions context, allowing multiple refresh operations within the refresh token lifetime. Implements security validation to prevent using expired or revoked tokens.

operations.description:
This endpoint enables users to obtain new access tokens when their current access token expires, without requiring them to re-enter their credentials and authenticate again. The user provides their refresh token obtained during initial login or previous refresh operation. The system validates the refresh token is properly formatted and has valid JWT signature.

The system verifies the refresh token has not expired (originally valid for 7 days from issue). If the refresh token has expired, the operation fails with error code AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED and message 'Your refresh token has expired. Please log in again.' The system extracts the user ID from the refresh token and verifies the user account still exists in todo_app_users table and has 'active' status. If the user account is inactive or deleted, refresh is denied.

The system verifies the refresh token belongs to an active session in todo_app_user_sessions table (expired_at is NULL, indicating session not yet terminated). If the session has been terminated or explicitly logged out, the refresh token is invalidated. Upon successful validation, the system generates and returns a new access token with 30-minute expiration, containing the user's ID, email, and 'user' role claim.

Optionally, the system may issue a new refresh token as well, extending the refresh cycle and keeping the user in an active state without requiring re-authentication. The response includes the new access token, optional new refresh token, their expiration times, and user information. User remains seamlessly authenticated with new access token valid for the next 30 minutes of activity.

If refresh token is invalid, malformed, or has invalid signature, the operation fails with error code AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN. If user cannot be found or has been deleted, the operation fails with error code AUTH_USER_NOT_FOUND. Refresh operations do not create new sessions - they extend the lifetime of the existing session through token renewal.

This operation does not require an active access token; the refresh token alone is sufficient. This allows users to maintain their session even when their access token has expired. Related operations include login (/auth/user/login) for initial authentication, logout (/auth/user/logout) for session termination, and account management operations requiring active access tokens.

operations.specification: Admin authentication operation for system administrators to authenticate and obtain JWT access token. Admins authenticate with email and password credentials to access the system and perform administrative functions. The operation validates admin credentials against stored password hash, creates an authenticated session, and issues a JWT token with admin role claim.

operations.description:
Admin login operation enables system administrators to authenticate with email and password. WHEN an admin submits credentials, THE system SHALL validate the email exists in the todo_app_admins table, verify the password_hash matches using secure comparison, and upon successful authentication create an admin session with enhanced security constraints (15-minute inactivity timeout). THE system SHALL issue a JWT access token containing admin role claim and permissions array. THE JWT token SHALL expire after 30 minutes of issuance.

Admin authentication differs from regular user authentication through enhanced security measures: admin sessions expire after 15 minutes of inactivity (compared to 30 minutes for users), all admin actions are logged in the todo_app_audit_logs immutable audit trail with action_type, description, before_value, after_value, and ip_address fields for accountability and compliance. Admin login attempts are monitored for security threats - after 5 failed login attempts within 15 minutes, the admin account is temporarily locked for 30 minutes.

IF admin credentials are invalid, THEN THE system SHALL deny access and return error code AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS without revealing whether email exists or password was incorrect. IF admin account status is not 'active', THEN THE system SHALL deny login and return error code AUTH_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE. IF admin session already exists from another location, THE system SHALL allow the login (concurrent admin sessions permitted) but optionally log the unusual access pattern.

Successful admin authentication triggers creation of todo_app_admin_sessions record capturing ip, href, referrer, created_at timestamp, and expired_at initially NULL. Admin can access all system features including user management (view todo_app_users list, change user status, delete user accounts and associated todos via cascade), system statistics, audit logs, backup and recovery operations, and administrative configuration.

responseBody.description: Admin authentication response with JWT access token

THE admin is automatically authenticated upon successful registration and issued a JWT access token containing admin role claim.

This operation allows prospective users to create a new Todo application account by submitting their email address and desired password. The system validates all input data according to security and business rules before creating the user account.

The email address must follow valid RFC 5322 format (e.g., user@example.com) and must not already be registered in the system. The password must be at least 8 characters long and will be securely hashed using bcrypt or equivalent before storage.

Upon successful registration, the system creates a new user record in the todo_app_users table with status set to 'active', automatically initializes the user's empty todo list, and generates a new authenticated session. The newly registered user is automatically logged in and receives a JWT authentication token valid for 30 minutes of inactivity, enabling immediate access to their personal todo dashboard without requiring a separate login step.

If registration fails due to validation errors (invalid email format, password too short, or duplicate email), the system rejects the request with specific error messages guiding the user on how to correct the problem. The registration process is atomic - either the complete user account is created with all necessary initialization, or the operation fails entirely with no partial account creation.

operations.description:
This operation enables registered users to authenticate into the Todo application by submitting their email address and password. The system verifies the credentials against the user account stored in the todo_app_users table and establishes an authenticated session upon successful verification.

The login process performs secure credential validation including email existence verification and password hash comparison using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. The system retrieves the user record by email address, verifies the provided plaintext password matches the stored password hash using bcrypt verification or equivalent, and confirms the user's account status is 'active' (not suspended or deleted).

Upon successful authentication, the system creates a new user session record in todo_app_user_sessions table with connection metadata (IP address, referrer URL), generates a JWT access token valid for 30 minutes of inactivity, and optionally generates a refresh token valid for 7 days. The authenticated user receives both tokens and is immediately redirected to their personal todo dashboard where they can view and manage their todos.

If authentication fails, the system implements security measures including tracking failed login attempts per email address. After 5 consecutive failed login attempts within 15 minutes, the system temporarily locks the account for 15 minutes, preventing further login attempts and requiring the user to use the password reset functionality. Failed login responses use generic error messages ('Email or password is incorrect') to prevent email enumeration attacks that could reveal which email addresses are registered in the system.

The operation ensures security by never revealing whether an email address is registered, implementing rate limiting on login attempts, recording session metadata for audit trail purposes, and invalidating all previous sessions if the user logs in from a new device.

operations.specification: This operation terminates the authenticated user's session, invalidating their JWT authentication token and requiring re-authentication for future access. The logout endpoint processes the POST request from an authenticated user, validates their session is active, invalidates the session token, clears session data, and returns confirmation. This operation is associated with the todo_app_user_sessions table which stores session records tracking authenticated user connections with JWT token references, connection metadata (IP, device info), and expiration tracking.
operations.summary: Terminate the authenticated user's session and invalidate their authentication token
operations.description:
This operation allows an authenticated user to terminate their current session and log out from the Todo application. When a user invokes logout, the system invalidates their JWT authentication token, terminates their active session, clears cached session data, and returns confirmation to the user.

The user must be properly authenticated with a valid JWT token to invoke this operation. The system verifies the token is not already expired and belongs to an active user session before processing the logout request.

After successful logout, the user's authentication token becomes invalid immediately and cannot be reused. Any subsequent API requests using the invalidated token will receive an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response, requiring the user to re-authenticate by logging in again.

The system records the session termination timestamp in the todo_app_user_sessions table, marking the session's expired_at field with the current UTC timestamp. This creates an audit trail of the logout action.

If the user attempts to logout while already logged out or with an expired token, the system returns an error indicating the session is already terminated or invalid. The operation is idempotent when attempted with an already-expired session.

Before processing logout, the system verifies the user making the request is the owner of the session being terminated, preventing unauthorized logout attempts on behalf of other users.

operations.specification: This operation enables users who have forgotten their password to reset it through a secure email-based recovery process. The password reset endpoint accepts a POST request with the user's email address, generates a secure time-limited password reset token, sends the token via email to the user, and validates the user's identity before allowing password change. This operation is associated with the todo_app_users table which stores user accounts with email addresses, secure password hashes, account status tracking, and temporal audit fields.
operations.summary: Initiate a password reset process via secure email token for users who forgot their password
operations.description:
This operation enables users who have forgotten their password to securely reset it through an email-based recovery mechanism. The operation supports two phases: (1) password reset request initiation and (2) password reset completion using a token.

Phase 1 - Reset Request: When a user initiates a password reset by providing their email address, the system validates that the email exists in the todo_app_users table, generates a cryptographically secure password reset token with a 1-hour expiration time, and sends the token to the user's email address. The system returns a generic confirmation message without revealing whether the email was found (for security purposes, to prevent email enumeration attacks).

Phase 2 - Reset Completion: When a user clicks the password reset link in their email and submits a new password, the system validates that the reset token is still valid and not expired, validates the new password meets security requirements (minimum 8 characters), hashes the new password using secure algorithms (bcrypt or Argon2), updates the user's password_hash in the database, invalidates all existing sessions for that user by setting expired_at timestamp in todo_app_user_sessions records, and returns a success confirmation.

The password reset process enforces strict security measures: tokens are single-use and time-limited (valid for exactly 1 hour), passwords are hashed before storage using secure algorithms, all existing user sessions are terminated after password change to force re-authentication, and the operation prevents password reuse by requiring new passwords to be different from current ones.

If the password reset token has expired or is invalid, the system displays an error message instructing the user to request a new password reset. If the user provides an invalid password that fails security requirements, the system displays specific feedback about which requirements are not met. If the email address is not found in the system, the system still displays a confirmation message (for security reasons).

After successful password reset, the user must log in again with their new password. The system does not automatically log the user in after password reset for security reasons. Users with soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at timestamp is set) are allowed to initiate password reset to enable account recovery.

requestBody.description: User's email address to initiate password reset, or password reset completion data with reset token and new password

responseBody.description: Confirmation message for password reset initiation or completion with appropriate status and guidance

operations.specification: This operation allows an authenticated user to change their account password. The user provides their current password for verification and a new password that meets security requirements. The system validates the current password is correct, verifies the new password meets minimum requirements (8+ characters), ensures the new password differs from the old password, and updates the password hash in the database. Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the user are invalidated, forcing re-authentication on next access. This operation maps to the todo_app_users table and implements password change workflow from requirement 02-user-actors-authentication.md section 'Account Security'.
operations.summary: Change authenticated user's account password
operations.description:
This operation enables an authenticated user to change their password from their current password to a new one. The user must provide their current password for verification purposes to ensure they have authorization to change the password. The system validates the current password against the stored password hash using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

The new password must meet the following requirements: minimum 8 characters in length. The new password must differ from the current password; users cannot set a password to the same value as before. The system rejects passwords that are identical to the previous password.

Upon successful password change, the system performs two critical security operations: (1) The password hash in the database is updated using bcrypt or Argon2 with a unique salt, and (2) All existing JWT tokens and session records for the user are invalidated after the success response is delivered. The current user session is preserved temporarily to allow the success response (HTTP 200) to be delivered to the client, then automatically expires after the response is transmitted. This forces the user to re-authenticate with their new password on their next request or page refresh, ensuring the password change is propagated across all sessions and all devices.

This operation is intended for authenticated users who want to change their own password. Administrators cannot use this operation to change other users' passwords; each user must change their own password directly. The operation includes comprehensive audit logging of the password change attempt (success or failure) for security purposes. Error responses provide specific feedback about why the password change failed (e.g., 'Current password incorrect', 'New password must be at least 8 characters', 'New password cannot be the same as current password').

requestBody.description: User's current password for verification and new password meeting security requirements

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful password change with user identity information

This operation retrieves the current authenticated user's active session information, including details about when they logged in, when their session will expire, and metadata about the session origin (IP address, referrer URL). The user must be authenticated with a valid JWT token to access this endpoint.

The system validates that the user's JWT token is still valid and has not expired. If the token is invalid or expired, the operation returns a 401 Unauthorized error with message 'Your session has expired. Please log in again.' The system then retrieves the corresponding session record from the database using the user ID extracted from the JWT token.

The response includes complete session information: (1) Current user's unique identifier and email address, (2) Session ID (unique identifier for this login session), (3) Session creation timestamp in UTC (when user logged in), (4) Session expiration timestamp in UTC (when session will automatically expire due to inactivity or timeout), (5) IP address from which the session was established, (6) HTTP referrer URL that led to the login, (7) Connection URL where session was initiated.

Users can use this information to verify they recognize the IP address and location from which they are logged in, supporting security awareness and helping detect unauthorized access. For admin users, this endpoint works identically but retrieves session information from todo_app_admin_sessions instead of todo_app_user_sessions, with the same response structure containing admin session details.

operations.description:
Create a new user account by registering with an email address and secure password. This operation implements the complete user registration workflow where new users can sign up for the Todo application by providing their authentication credentials. The system validates the email format, ensures the email is unique across all registered user accounts, and enforces password security requirements before creating the account.

When a user submits registration information, the operation performs comprehensive validation of all input fields. The email address must follow valid email format (RFC 5322 standard) and must not already exist in the system - duplicate email registration is rejected with error message indicating the email is already in use. The password must meet minimum security requirements (at least 8 characters) to ensure account security and prevent brute force attacks.

Security considerations are critical for this operation. Passwords are never stored in plaintext; instead, the system generates a secure hash using bcrypt with appropriate cost factor or Argon2 hashing algorithm before storing. Each password is hashed with a unique salt to prevent rainbow table attacks. The hashing occurs server-side, never trusting client-provided hash values. The operation also implements rate limiting on registration attempts to prevent abuse and automated account creation attacks.

Upon successful registration, the operation creates a user record in the todo_app_users table with automatically-generated unique user ID (UUID), the provided email address (normalized to lowercase), the hashed password, account status set to 'active' (enabling immediate login), and system-generated creation timestamp in UTC. The operation returns the newly created user account information but NEVER returns the password hash in the response for security.

If registration fails due to validation errors (invalid email format, duplicate email, weak password, missing fields), the operation rejects the request with specific error messages indicating which validation failed and how to correct it. No partial user record is created if any validation fails - the operation is atomic, either fully succeeding or fully failing.

This operation is public and does not require authentication, allowing unregistered users to create new accounts. However, after successful registration, the user must authenticate with their credentials using the login operation to access their personal todo list.

operations.summary: Permanently delete a user account and all associated todos
operations.description:
This operation allows an admin to delete a user account from the system. When executed, the system performs a soft delete by recording the deletion timestamp (deleted_at field in todo_app_users table), which prevents the user from logging in and marks the account as deleted for compliance purposes.

The deletion operation cascades to all related records: all todos owned by the user are permanently removed from the database, all active sessions for that user are terminated immediately, and audit logs record the deletion action with the admin's ID, timestamp, and IP address for security accountability.

⚠️ **WARNING**: This operation is irreversible. All todos owned by this user will be permanently deleted. All active sessions will be terminated immediately. This sensitive administrative function should only be performed when absolutely necessary and with explicit administrative justification.

Security and authorization are critical for this operation. The system verifies the requesting user has admin role before allowing deletion. The operation requires explicit admin confirmation due to its irreversible nature - once a user and their data are deleted, recovery is only possible through database backup restore. The system logs all deletion attempts (both successful and failed) in the audit trail as specified in 07-admin-features.md.

From the database perspective, the user record in todo_app_users is marked with a deleted_at timestamp rather than permanently removed, allowing for audit trail preservation and potential recovery within the backup retention window. All related todo_app_todos records owned by that user are cascade-deleted. All active sessions in todo_app_user_sessions are terminated. The audit_logs table records this admin action with complete details.

It supports complex query parameters for filtering by status (active/completed), priority level (low/medium/high), due date ranges, and text search across todo titles and descriptions. operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of todos with advanced filtering options
operations.description:
This operation provides comprehensive todo list retrieval with advanced filtering, searching, and pagination capabilities. When an authenticated user requests their todo list through this endpoint, the system retrieves todos from the todo_app_todos table that belong to the authenticated user (matching todo_app_user_id), applies any requested filters, and returns paginated results.

The operation supports multiple filtering dimensions to help users organize and find their todos effectively. Users can filter by status (active or completed), priority level (low, medium, high), due date ranges, and search by text matching in todo title and description fields using full-text search capabilities with GIN trigram indexes. Filters can be combined to narrow results further. The request body should specify filter criteria (status, priority, date_from, date_to), search terms (title_search, description_search), sort preferences (sort_by, sort_order), and pagination parameters (page, limit with maximum 100 items per page).

Pagination is implemented to handle users with large numbers of todos efficiently. The system supports configurable page size (default 20 items per page, maximum 100 items per page) and offset-based pagination to prevent memory issues with large result sets. Response includes metadata about total count, current page, total pages, and available sorting options.

Sorting options allow users to organize results by creation date (newest first by default), due date (earliest deadlines first), completion status (active first), priority level (high first), or modification date. Multiple sort criteria can be applied with primary and secondary sort fields specified in the request.

From a database perspective, the system executes indexed queries against todo_app_todos table using the indexes on (todo_app_user_id, created_at), (todo_app_user_id, status), (todo_app_user_id, due_date), and full-text search indexes on title and description fields (GIN trigram indexes) to ensure query performance remains under 2 seconds even for users with thousands of todos. Data isolation ensures users can only see their own todos - the query automatically filters by matching todo_app_user_id with the authenticated user's ID.

The response includes complete todo details (ID, title, description, status, priority, due date, created timestamp, updated timestamp, completed timestamp if applicable) organized by the user's requested sort order and pagination. Completed todos are clearly marked with completion timestamps. Status indicators show whether each todo is 'active' or 'completed'. This operation respects strict data isolation requirements - users cannot access or discover other users' todos through any filtering or search mechanism.

requestBody.description: Search criteria (title and description search terms), filtering options (status, priority, due date range), sorting preferences (sort field, order), and pagination parameters (page number, page size)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo items matching search and filter criteria with pagination metadata (total count, current page, page size, total pages)

operations.summary: Create a new todo item with title and optional details
operations.description:
Creates a new todo item for the authenticated user. The user provides a required title (maximum 255 characters) that describes what needs to be done, and may optionally provide a detailed description (maximum 2000 characters), priority level (low/medium/high), and future due date (ISO 8601 format, cannot be in past). The system validates all input fields according to business rules specified in 06-business-rules.md.

The system automatically assigns the todo to the authenticated user exclusively, ensuring data isolation. Only the owner of the todo can view, modify, or delete it. The system generates a unique identifier, sets the initial status to 'active' (incomplete), records the creation timestamp, and initializes the modification timestamp to match creation time.

After successful creation, the todo is immediately available in the user's todo list and can be viewed, updated, or deleted through subsequent API operations. The completion timestamp is not set until the user explicitly marks the todo as completed.

This operation enforces strong validation on all input fields: title cannot be empty and cannot exceed 255 characters; description if provided cannot exceed 2000 characters; priority if provided must be one of the three valid values; due date if provided must be in valid ISO 8601 date format and cannot represent a date in the past. If any validation fails, the operation is rejected and appropriate error messages are returned to guide the user.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated audit logs of all administrative actions with filtering and sorting
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of audit trail records documenting all administrative actions performed on the Todo system. This operation provides comprehensive visibility into what admins have done, when they did it, from where, and what changed as a result.

The audit trail serves multiple critical purposes: security monitoring to detect unauthorized or suspicious admin actions, compliance tracking to demonstrate system governance, investigation of incidents or issues by tracking the sequence of admin operations, and accountability by recording which admin performed each action with timestamp and IP address.

This operation queries the immutable todo_app_audit_logs table which implements append-only logging - entries are never modified or deleted, ensuring the audit trail cannot be tampered with. Each log entry captures complete context: the admin who performed the action (todo_app_admin_id), the type of action performed (action_type like 'user_deleted', 'user_status_changed'), the affected resource (target_user_id if a user was involved), before and after values showing what changed, IP address for location tracking, and timestamp in UTC.

The operation supports powerful filtering capabilities to locate specific events: filter by action type to find all user deletions or status changes, filter by date range to investigate activities within a time window, search by description text to find actions related to specific keywords, filter by affected user to see all actions impacting a particular user, or filter by admin to audit a specific admin's activities.

Response includes pagination metadata to navigate large datasets efficiently. Admin users can export or generate reports from audit log data for compliance purposes.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of activity records showing all user operations performed on the Todo system. This operation provides comprehensive visibility into how the system is being used by tracking user interactions and operations for monitoring and analytics purposes.

Activity logs serve operational monitoring and system usage analysis: understanding which operations are most commonly used by users, identifying peak usage times and patterns, monitoring active user counts and session activity, tracking system load and performance characteristics, detecting potential security issues through behavioral pattern analysis, and generating usage statistics and analytics reports.

Unlike audit logs which focus on admin actions, activity logs track regular user operations such as todo creation, modification, deletion, status changes, and login/logout events. Each log entry captures: timestamp in UTC, user who performed the action, operation type (create_todo, update_todo, delete_todo, mark_complete, etc.), any relevant details about the operation, and result/status.

The operation supports comprehensive filtering to analyze different aspects of system usage: filter by operation type to analyze usage of specific features (e.g., how many todos are deleted vs completed), filter by date range to analyze usage over time periods, filter by user to track individual user behavior, or filter by result status to find failed operations that may indicate problems.

Response includes pagination metadata and aggregate statistics (if applicable) such as total operations in period, operation type distribution, active user count, and performance metrics. Activity logs enable admins to monitor system health, identify optimization opportunities, and understand user behavior patterns.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a list of all system backups that have been created. It operates on the backup management system and provides administrators with visibility into available backup snapshots for disaster recovery and data restoration purposes. operations.summary: Retrieve list of system backups
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all system backups available in the system. This operation allows administrators to view backup snapshots that can be used for data restoration and disaster recovery.

Each backup record includes the timestamp when the backup was created, the size of the backup, verification status indicating whether the backup is valid and restorable, and the completion status of the backup process. The list is sorted by creation date with most recent backups appearing first.

This is an admin-only operation requiring elevated permissions. When an administrator accesses this endpoint, the system logs the access attempt in the audit trail for security and compliance purposes. Administrators can use this information to understand backup coverage and identify which backups are available for recovery in case of data loss or system failure.

The operation supports filtering and pagination to handle large numbers of backups. Administrators can retrieve backups from specific date ranges or search for backups meeting certain criteria. Each backup record shows whether it has been verified as valid and restorable.

operations.specification: This operation initiates a new system backup operation to capture the current state of all system data. It operates on the backup management system and creates a point-in-time snapshot of the entire application database and user data. The operation validates admin authorization, initiates the backup process, and returns confirmation of the backup initiation with backup metadata.
operations.summary: Initiate new system backup
operations.description:
Initiate creation of a new system backup to capture the current state of all application data. This operation allows administrators to manually trigger backup operations for on-demand data protection and disaster recovery preparation.

When a backup is initiated, the system creates a point-in-time snapshot of the entire database including all user accounts, todos, sessions, and audit logs. The backup process runs asynchronously in the background while maintaining full system availability for users. The system does not interrupt normal user operations during backup execution.

The backup operation captures all data needed to restore the system to the exact state at the time the backup was initiated. The system automatically encrypts the backup for security and stores it in a durable location separate from production systems. Backup integrity is automatically verified after completion to ensure the backup is valid and can be used for restoration if needed.

This is an admin-only operation requiring elevated permissions. When an administrator initiates a backup, the system logs the action in the audit trail with the timestamp, admin ID, and backup ID. The operation returns confirmation with the newly created backup ID, creation timestamp, and estimated completion time for the administrator's reference.

The system maintains a retention policy of at least 7 days of daily backups to enable recovery from data corruption or accidental deletion up to one week in the past. Administrators should monitor backup creation to ensure regular successful backups are occurring.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of backup initiation with metadata about the newly created backup

operations.specification: This operation allows an authenticated admin user to restore the Todo application to a previous state by selecting a backup file created by the system. The backup identified by backupId contains a complete snapshot of the system state at a specific point in time. Restoration is a sensitive operation that will overwrite current application data with the backed-up version, rolling back all changes made after the backup was created. This operation is admin-only and requires explicit confirmation before execution. The operation writes the backup data back to the primary database, making it available to all users with the rolled-back state. Implementation must verify backup integrity before restoration begins. The operation logs the restoration action in the audit trail with admin ID, timestamp, and backup details for compliance and security purposes.
operations.summary: Restore the system from a backup file to a previous state
operations.description:
This admin-only operation restores the entire Todo application from a previously created backup. The system will revert all data to the exact state captured in the backup identified by backupId.

The backup restoration process involves verifying the backup integrity, ensuring data consistency, and writing all backed-up data to the production database. During restoration, the system will be temporarily unavailable to users. All application data created or modified after the backup timestamp will be lost and replaced with the backed-up versions.

This operation requires admin authentication and explicit confirmation due to its destructive nature. The admin must verify they have selected the correct backup before confirming the restoration. The system will validate the backup exists, is not corrupted, and can be successfully restored before committing to the operation.

After successful restoration, all users will see the application state as it existed when the backup was created. The restoration action is logged in the admin audit trail with complete details including the admin ID, timestamp, backup ID, and any error conditions encountered during restoration. Users will need to log in again after the restoration completes.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves all active sessions for the currently authenticated user or admin. The sessions table tracks login history and active connections across devices and browsers. Each session includes metadata about when it was created, what IP address it originated from, and whether it is still active (not yet expired). This operation supports both regular users retrieving their own sessions and admins viewing all sessions in the system for monitoring purposes. The response includes session IDs, creation timestamps, IP addresses, device/referrer information, and expiration status. Admins can use this to track user activity and detect suspicious login patterns. Regular users can see all their active sessions across devices and manually terminate sessions if desired.
operations.summary: Retrieve all active sessions for the authenticated user or view all system sessions for admins
operations.description:
This operation retrieves session information depending on the authenticated user's role. For regular users, it returns all sessions associated with their account, showing active and expired sessions. Each session record includes the timestamp when the session was established, the IP address used to authenticate, the browser/device information via referrer data, and the URL where the session was created.

For admin users, this operation returns all sessions across the entire system - both user sessions and admin sessions - providing administrators with visibility into who is currently logged in, from where, and for how long. This enables admins to monitor for suspicious login patterns, detect unauthorized access attempts, and manage user sessions if needed.

The response includes complete session metadata: session ID (unique identifier), user/admin ID, creation timestamp in UTC, expiration timestamp (NULL for active sessions), IP address, connection URL, and referrer. Sessions that have expired (where expired_at is populated) indicate previous login sessions that are no longer active. Sessions with NULL expired_at are currently active and the user/admin is logged in.

This operation helps track user activity across devices, enables detection of concurrent sessions, and provides the security foundation for session management and audit logging. The list is ordered chronologically with most recent sessions first.

operations.specification: This operation provides user session logout functionality by invalidating the current user's active authentication session. The DELETE method on the /sessions endpoint terminates the user's JWT token, clears session state, and prevents further authenticated requests with the invalidated token. This operation requires active authentication (valid JWT token in Authorization header). Upon successful logout, the user must re-authenticate with email and password to access protected resources. The operation integrates with the todo_app_user_sessions table to mark the session as expired by setting the expired_at timestamp. This is a critical security operation that completes the user authentication lifecycle and ensures proper session cleanup.
operations.summary: Logout the authenticated user by terminating their active session
operations.description:
This operation allows an authenticated user to logout and terminate their current session. When a user initiates logout, the system marks their active session as expired and invalidates their JWT authentication token.

The logout operation performs the following steps: (1) verifies the user has valid authentication credentials, (2) retrieves the current user's active session from the database, (3) sets the expired_at timestamp on the session record to mark it as terminated, (4) invalidates the JWT token so future requests with this token are rejected, (5) clears any session data stored in memory or cache, (6) returns a success confirmation to the user.

From a security perspective, logout is critical for ensuring users can explicitly terminate their sessions. This prevents unauthorized access if a device is left unattended or if a user's session token is compromised. Sessions are also automatically terminated after 30 minutes of inactivity or when the user changes their password (forcing re-authentication on all devices).

The operation targets the todo_app_user_sessions table to record the session termination. The user who is logged out is identified from the current authentication context (JWT token claims). No request body is required; the system determines which session to logout based on the authentication token in the request header.

If the user is not currently authenticated or their session is already expired, the system returns an appropriate error. Successful logout returns HTTP 200 OK with confirmation message indicating the session has been terminated and the user must re-authenticate for future requests.

ITodoAppUser.description:
Represents a user account in the Todo application. This entity contains the user's authentication credentials, account status, and temporal audit information. Users are the primary actors in the system who authenticate and manage their own todo lists. Each user has a unique email address for authentication, a securely hashed password, account status tracking, and timestamps recording account creation, modification, and soft deletion events.

Users form one-to-many relationships with todos (one user can have many todos) and sessions (one user can have many active sessions). The user entity is central to data isolation - all todos are owned exclusively by one user and access is strictly enforced through user ID verification.

Account status determines whether the user can currently access the system: 'active' allows normal login and use, 'inactive' prevents login but preserves account data. The deleted_at timestamp implements soft delete functionality where deleted accounts are marked but preserved for audit trail purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. This UUID is automatically generated by the system when the user registers and serves as the primary key for identifying this user throughout the application. The ID is immutable after creation and is used in all references to this user from other entities like todos and sessions. The ID establishes ownership relationships - todos reference the user ID to indicate which user owns them.

email.description: User's email address serving as the unique authentication identifier. This email must be unique across all user accounts in the system - no two users can register with the same email address. The email is used as the login identifier when users authenticate. Email addresses must follow RFC 5322 standard email format (e.g., user@example.com). Email addresses are normalized to lowercase for storage and comparison purposes to prevent duplicate registrations of the same email with different cases.

oneOf.description: Current account status indicating whether the user can access the system. Valid values are 'active' (user can log in and use the application) and 'inactive' (user cannot log in but account data is preserved). Accounts default to 'active' when first created. Admins can change user status to suspend access without deleting account data. When status is 'inactive', all login attempts are rejected with appropriate error message.

Valid values are 'active' (user can log in and use the application) and 'inactive' (user cannot log in but account data is preserved). Accounts default to 'active' when first created. Admins can change user status to suspend access without deleting account data. When status is 'inactive', all login attempts are rejected with appropriate error message.

Valid values are 'active' (user can log in and use the application) and 'inactive' (user cannot log in but account data is preserved). Accounts default to 'active' when first created. Admins can change user status to suspend access without deleting account data. When status is 'inactive', all login attempts are rejected with appropriate error message.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the user account was created and registered. This timestamp is automatically generated by the system during account creation and is immutable - it never changes after initial creation regardless of subsequent account modifications. Created_at provides a historical record of when the user first joined the system and is used for sorting users by registration date or identifying new users.

updated_at.description: Timestamp in UTC of the most recent modification to any user account field. This timestamp is automatically updated by the system whenever any property of the user account is changed (email update, status change, etc.). Updated_at is distinct from created_at and enables tracking of account activity and modifications. The timestamp reflects the time of the most recent change, allowing identification of recently modified accounts.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp in UTC indicating soft deletion of the user account. When NULL (empty), the account is active and accessible. When populated with a timestamp, the account is marked as deleted but data is preserved in the database for audit trail, compliance, and potential recovery purposes. Soft-deleted users cannot log in and their account appears as deleted to admins, but all associated data and history remains in the system. Hard deletion of user data may occur after a retention period (typically 30 days) following the soft delete timestamp.

email.description: User's email address for the new account. Must follow valid email format per RFC 5322 standard (e.g., user@example.com). Must not already be registered in the system. This email address will be used as the unique login identifier for the new user account.

The backend receives this plain text password, hashes it securely using bcrypt algorithm, and stores only the hash in the database for security.

The email must be in valid format and not already registered. The password is validated to meet minimum length requirements (8+ characters) and is securely hashed using bcrypt before being stored in the database.

Upon successful registration, the new user account is created with 'active' status in the todo_app_users table, creation timestamp is recorded in UTC, and the user is automatically authenticated with JWT tokens (access token expires in 30 minutes, refresh token expires in 7 days). The user immediately gains access to create, view, update, and delete their own todo items without requiring a separate login step.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description:
Successful authentication response providing the authenticated user's information and JWT tokens for session management. Returned after successful login (POST /auth/user/login) or token refresh (POST /auth/user/refresh) operations.

Contains the authenticated user's ID and email from todo_app_users table, current account status (must be 'active' for successful authentication), and JWT token information required for continued authenticated access.

The token object contains both the access_token (30-minute expiration) and refresh_token (7-day expiration) which must be used for subsequent authenticated API requests. The access_token must be included in the Authorization header for all subsequent authenticated API requests: 'Authorization: Bearer [access_token]'. The refresh_token is used to obtain new access tokens before expiration without requiring re-authentication.

Both tokens are cryptographically signed JWT tokens that cannot be modified by the client. Token expiration timestamps are provided to allow the client to proactively refresh the access token before it expires, enabling seamless user experience without unexpected 401 Unauthorized responses.

email.description: User's email address for authentication. Must follow valid email format (RFC 5322, e.g., user@example.com). This is the unique login identifier for the user account registered in the todo_app_users table.

password.description: User's plaintext password for authentication verification. The system receives this plain text password, validates it against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_users table using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. Password should be at least 8 characters long. Never transmitted in plaintext over unencrypted connections - HTTPS/TLS encryption is mandatory.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the login request originates. Optional field - server can extract from request header if not provided. Used for session tracking, security monitoring, and audit trail in todo_app_user_sessions table. Captured for detecting suspicious access patterns and geographic anomalies.

href.description: Connection URL / request URL representing the entry point when the user initiates login. This is the page URL where the login request was submitted from. MANDATORY for session context and used in todo_app_user_sessions table for audit trail. Example: 'https://todoapp.example.com/login'

referrer.description: HTTP Referrer URL indicating the source page that led to the login page. MANDATORY for session context. Captured in todo_app_user_sessions for tracking traffic sources and user journey analysis. Helps identify where users came from before logging in.

ITodoAppUser.ILogin.description:
User login request with authentication credentials and connection metadata. Contains the email address and password for verifying the user's identity. The system validates the email exists in the todo_app_users table, retrieves the associated password_hash, and verifies the provided plaintext password against the stored hash using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks.

The connection metadata (href, referrer) is MANDATORY for session context as required for self-authentication operations per requirements 6.5.1. The ip address is optional as the server can extract it from the request. After successful authentication validation, the system creates a new session record in the todo_app_user_sessions table with this metadata and generates JWT access/refresh tokens.

Security measures include: lockout after 5 failed attempts within 15 minutes, constant-time password comparison, secure transmission over HTTPS/TLS only, session tracking by IP and referrer for anomaly detection, and comprehensive audit logging of all login attempts.

refresh_token.description: Valid refresh token previously issued during user login or previous token refresh operation. The refresh token contains the user's ID and has a 7-day expiration window. The system validates the token signature, verifies it has not expired, extracts the user ID, and confirms the user account still exists in todo_app_users table with 'active' status. Must be a properly formatted JWT token with valid cryptographic signature. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or malformed, token refresh operation fails with error code AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN or AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED.

ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.description:
User token refresh request for obtaining new access tokens. Contains the refresh token from the previous login or token refresh operation. The system validates the refresh token is properly formatted and has a valid JWT signature that matches the server's signing key.

The system verifies the refresh token has not expired (originally valid for 7 days from issue). If expired, operation fails with error AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRED. The system extracts the user ID from the token and verifies the user account exists in todo_app_users table and has 'active' status. The system verifies the refresh token belongs to an active session in todo_app_user_sessions table with expired_at as NULL.

Upon successful validation, the system generates and returns a new access token (30-minute expiration) and optionally a new refresh token (7-day expiration). This operation enables seamless session continuation without requiring users to re-enter credentials when access tokens expire. No new session record is created; token refresh extends the existing session through token renewal.

email.description: Administrator's email address used for authentication. Must be unique across all admin accounts and match exactly (case-insensitive) an email in the todo_app_admins table. The system will verify this email exists before checking the password. If email does not exist, authentication fails with generic error message.

password.description: Administrator's plaintext password for authentication. THE system SHALL hash this password server-side using bcrypt or Argon2 and compare against the stored password_hash in the todo_app_admins table. Password is never stored in plaintext anywhere. Must be at least 8 characters for the account to be valid. Clients MUST transmit this over HTTPS/TLS encryption only.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the login request originates. Optional field - server can extract from request header if not provided. Used for session tracking, security monitoring, and audit trail in todo_app_admin_sessions table. Captured for detecting suspicious access patterns and geographic anomalies.

href.description: Connection URL / request URL representing the entry point when the admin initiates login. This is the page URL where the login request was submitted from. MANDATORY for session context and used in todo_app_admin_sessions table for audit trail. Example: 'https://todoapp.example.com/login'

referrer.description: HTTP Referrer URL indicating the source page that led to the login page. MANDATORY for session context. Captured in todo_app_admin_sessions for tracking traffic sources and user journey analysis. Helps identify where admins came from before logging in.

ITodoAppAdmin.ILogin.description:
Admin login request containing credentials for authentication. WHEN an admin submits login credentials, THE system SHALL validate the email exists in todo_app_admins table, verify the password matches the stored password_hash using secure comparison to prevent timing attacks, and upon successful authentication create a todo_app_admin_sessions record and issue JWT access token.

The email is the unique login identifier. Password is validated server-side against the stored bcrypt or Argon2 hash. Upon successful validation, a JWT access token is issued with admin role claim and 30-minute expiration. An admin session is created capturing connection metadata (IP address, href URL, referrer URL) for audit trail and security monitoring.

IF credentials are invalid, THEN THE system SHALL deny access and return error AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS without revealing whether email exists or password was incorrect (for security). IF admin account status is not 'active', THEN THE system SHALL deny access with error AUTH_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE. After 5 failed login attempts within 15 minutes from the same email, THE system SHALL temporarily lock the admin account for 30 minutes as a security measure against brute force attacks.

This ID is immutable and assigned by the system during admin account creation. Never changes throughout the admin's lifetime in the system.
