Admin authorization response returned upon successful admin registration or login. Contains the authenticated admin's unique identifier and JWT token information needed for subsequent authenticated requests.

Response Structure: This response is issued after successful validation of admin registration credentials. The response confirms that the admin account was created successfully (or authenticated successfully in login case) and provides tokens needed for the admin to make authenticated requests.

Token Information: THE access token is valid for 30 minutes from issuance. THE refresh token is valid for 7 days from issuance. When the access token expires, the admin can use the refresh token to obtain a new access token without re-entering credentials (via the /auth/admin/refresh endpoint).

Admin Role & Permissions: The JWT access token includes admin role claim ('admin') which grants the authenticated admin permission to: view all user accounts in todo_app_users table including email, status, creation/update dates; delete specific user accounts (cascade deletes associated todos from todo_app_todos); view system-wide statistics and usage metrics; access and view immutable todo_app_audit_logs; modify system configuration settings; perform backup and recovery operations; view audit trail of all admin actions with admin ID, timestamp, affected user, action type, and details.

Token Usage: THE access token must be included in the Authorization header of all subsequent authenticated requests: 'Authorization: Bearer [access_token]'. The system validates the token signature, expiration, and admin role claim on every authenticated request.

email.description:
Admin's email address for authentication and administrative communication. Must follow valid email format (RFC 5322 standard, e.g., admin@example.com). Unique across all admin accounts - the system SHALL validate that no other admin account uses this email address. Used as the login identifier for admin authentication.

Validation: Must be in valid email format with at least one character before '@', valid domain name, and valid extension. Examples of valid formats: admin@company.com, admin.user@organization.co.uk. Examples of invalid formats: notanemail, admin@, @domain.com.

password.description:
Admin's plaintext password for authentication. Minimum 8 characters required. The system SHALL hash this password using bcrypt (cost factor ≥ 12) or Argon2 before storage. NEVER stored in plaintext - the plaintext password is received in the request, hashed server-side, and the hash is stored in the password_hash column of todo_app_admins table.

Password Requirements: Minimum 8 characters in length, may contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters. The system validates password meets minimum length requirement and rejects passwords shorter than 8 characters with error 'Password must be at least 8 characters long'.

Field Mapping: This DTO field 'password' maps to the Prisma model's 'password_hash' column. The plaintext password received here is hashed and stored in password_hash column.

password_confirmation.description:
Confirmation of the admin's password for verification during registration. Must exactly match the 'password' field. The system validates that both password fields match character-for-character before proceeding with account creation.

Validation: THE system SHALL verify password and password_confirmation fields match exactly. IF passwords do not match, THEN THE system SHALL reject registration with error code AUTH_PASSWORD_MISMATCH and display message 'Passwords do not match. Please re-enter your password'.

Usage: Used only during registration to prevent typos in password entry. Not sent during login operations.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRegister.description:
Admin registration request body for creating new administrator accounts during system initialization or by existing admins. Captures essential authentication credentials (email and password) needed to establish admin identity and access rights.

Registration Process: WHEN a registration request is submitted with this DTO, THE system SHALL validate email is in valid email format and does not already exist in todo_app_admins table (checking email uniqueness). THE system SHALL validate password meets minimum length requirement (8 characters). THE system SHALL verify password and password_confirmation match exactly.

Upon successful validation, THE system SHALL create new admin record in todo_app_admins table with: unique id (UUID generated by system), submitted email, password_hash (securely hashed from plaintext password), status automatically set to 'active', created_at and updated_at set to current UTC timestamp, deleted_at as NULL.

Authentication & Session Creation: THE admin is automatically authenticated upon successful registration and issued JWT access token containing admin role claim ('admin'). The system creates initial todo_app_admin_sessions record capturing connection metadata (ip address, href/request URL, referrer URL, created_at timestamp, expired_at as NULL for active session).

Admin Privileges Granted: Upon successful registration, the new admin immediately gains access to all administrative functions: view and manage user accounts in todo_app_users table, delete user accounts (which cascades deletion of associated todos from todo_app_todos), view system statistics, access immutable todo_app_audit_logs audit trail, and perform system maintenance including backups and configuration changes.

Error Scenarios: IF email already exists in todo_app_admins table, THEN THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS and message 'This email is already registered as an admin account'. IF password shorter than 8 characters, THEN THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_WEAK_PASSWORD. IF passwords do not match, THEN THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_PASSWORD_MISMATCH. IF email format is invalid, THEN THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_INVALID_EMAIL_FORMAT.

refresh_token.description:
Valid JWT refresh token obtained from previous authentication (admin registration or login). Used to obtain new access_token when current access_token expires. Valid for 7 days from issuance.

Token Source: This refresh_token is provided in ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized response from successful admin registration or login operations. Client stores this token securely (ideally in HttpOnly, Secure cookie) for future refresh operations.

Validation: THE system SHALL validate that refresh_token exists, has not been revoked, and the expiration timestamp (exp claim in JWT) has not passed (refresh tokens valid for 7 days from issuance). THE system SHALL verify the admin account referenced in the refresh_token still exists in todo_app_admins table with status 'active' (not 'inactive' or deleted with deleted_at set).

Token Validity Window: Refresh tokens are valid for 7 days from issuance. After 7 days, the refresh_token cannot be used and the admin must re-authenticate using login operation with email and password.

Format: JWT format with three base64-encoded segments separated by periods (header.payload.signature). Contains admin id, refresh_token_id, and exp (expiration) claim with Unix timestamp.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Admin token refresh request body for obtaining new JWT access token using valid refresh token. Sent when admin's current access_token expires (after 30 minutes) but refresh_token is still valid (within 7 days).

Refresh Operation: WHEN an admin submits a refresh token request with this DTO, THE system SHALL validate the refresh_token has not been revoked, and the expiration timestamp has not passed (refresh tokens valid for 7 days from issuance). THE system SHALL verify the admin account referenced in the refresh_token still exists in todo_app_admins table with status 'active'.

Success Response: IF validation passes, THE system SHALL issue new ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized response containing new JWT access_token with admin role claim and 30-minute expiration. THE system optionally issues new refresh_token extending the session (7-day validity).

Error Handling: IF refresh_token is invalid (malformed, wrong signature), THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN. IF refresh_token is expired (beyond 7-day window), THE system SHALL reject with error AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED and display message 'Your session has expired. Please log in again'. IF associated admin account is no longer active in todo_app_admins (status not 'active' or deleted_at is set), THEN THE system SHALL reject the refresh request with error AUTH_USER_INACTIVE and message 'Your admin account is no longer active. Please contact system administrator'.

Audit Logging: Admin refresh token requests are NOT logged to todo_app_audit_logs (authentication maintenance operations are not audit-logged). However, if admin subsequently performs administrative actions after refresh, those actions ARE logged in audit_logs with admin's ID, action type, timestamp, and other audit context.

Token Lifecycle: After refresh succeeds, the previous access_token becomes invalid but can still be revoked if needed for security. The new access_token can be used immediately in Authorization header for subsequent requests.

email.description: User's email address for authentication and account identification. Must follow valid email format (RFC 5322 standard, e.g., user@example.com). The system validates email format and ensures uniqueness - no two accounts can be created with the same email address. Email is normalized to lowercase for storage and comparison purposes. Required for account creation.

password.description: User's plaintext password for account authentication. Minimum 8 characters required for security. Submitted as plain text from the client during registration; the backend receives this plaintext password, validates it against security requirements, and hashes it using bcrypt or Argon2 before storing in the database as password_hash. Never stored or transmitted in plaintext after server-side hashing. Required for account creation. The actual password_hash database column is not exposed in any API response for security.

ITodoAppUser.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new user account during registration. Captures the minimum required information needed to establish a user account: email address for unique identification and login, and password for authentication.

The email must be provided in valid format and must not already exist in the system. The password must meet minimum length requirements (8+ characters) for account security. Other user properties like status (defaults to 'active'), account timestamps (system-generated), and deletion status (defaults to not deleted) are automatically set by the system and not provided in this creation request.

Upon successful registration, the system creates a user record with the provided email, securely hashes the provided password, sets status to 'active', records creation and update timestamps, and returns the complete created user object (without exposing the password hash).

email.description: User's email address for authentication and login identification. Must follow valid email format (RFC 5322 standard). Used as the unique login identifier for the user account in the todo_app_users table.

password.description: User's plaintext password for authentication verification during login. Minimum 8 characters required. The system securely hashes this password using bcrypt or equivalent and compares it against the stored password_hash field in the todo_app_users table using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. The plaintext password is never stored in the database.

ITodoAppUser.IRequest.description: Login request containing user credentials for authentication. Used when an authenticated user attempts to verify their identity by submitting their registered email address and plaintext password. The system validates these credentials against the todo_app_users table, verifies the email exists, and uses secure password verification against the stored password_hash. Upon successful authentication, the system creates a new session record in todo_app_user_sessions table and issues a JWT access token for subsequent authenticated requests.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating the user has been successfully logged out. Typical message: 'You have been successfully logged out.' This confirms that the user's session has been terminated and their JWT authentication token has been invalidated.

success.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the logout operation completed successfully. Value true indicates the session was properly terminated, all tokens have been invalidated, and the user is no longer authenticated. The authenticated user's session record in todo_app_user_sessions table has been marked with the expired_at timestamp.

ITodoAppLogoutResponse.description: Response returned after a user successfully logs out from the Todo application. Confirms that the user's session has been terminated, their JWT authentication token has been invalidated, and they are no longer authenticated to the system. After logout, any subsequent requests using the invalidated token will receive HTTP 401 Unauthorized response, requiring the user to re-authenticate by logging in again. The todo_app_user_sessions table record for this session will have its expired_at field populated with the logout timestamp.

email.description: User's email address for password reset initiation. Must be a valid email format (RFC 5322 standard) and exist as a registered account in the todo_app_users table. Used to identify which user account needs password reset and to send the password reset token via email. Required for Phase 1 (password reset request initiation). Can be omitted for Phase 2 (password reset completion). Example: 'john@example.com'

reset_token.description: Secure password reset token sent to user's email address. Generated by the system using cryptographically secure random data and valid for exactly 1 hour from generation. Must be submitted along with new_password to complete the password reset process. Required for Phase 2 (password reset completion). Can be omitted for Phase 1 (password reset request initiation). If token is expired or invalid, the system rejects the request with error code 'PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED' or 'PASSWORD_RESET_INVALID_TOKEN'.

new_password.description: New password for the user account. Must be at least 8 characters long and at most 256 characters. Will be hashed using bcrypt or Argon2 with unique salt before storage in the password_hash field of todo_app_users table. Must be different from the current password (system rejects if new password matches previous password). Required for Phase 2 (password reset completion). Can be omitted for Phase 1 (password reset request initiation). The password is hashed server-side; client must send plaintext password which the backend hashes before database storage.

confirm_password.description: Password confirmation field to verify user typed new_password correctly. Must match new_password exactly (character-for-character comparison). Used for Phase 2 (password reset completion) to prevent typos in password entry. Can be omitted for Phase 1 (password reset request initiation). If confirm_password does not match new_password, system displays error 'PASSWORD_MISMATCH' with message 'Passwords do not match. Please re-enter your password.'

ITodoAppAuthPasswordResetRequest.description:
Request body for password reset operations with two distinct phases.

Phase 1 - Password Reset Initiation: User provides their email address to request a password reset. The system validates the email exists in the todo_app_users table and sends a password reset token to the user's email address. The email field is required for this phase.

Phase 2 - Password Reset Completion: User provides the password reset token received via email and a new password. The system validates the token is valid and not expired, validates the new password meets security requirements (minimum 8 characters), and updates the user's password_hash in the database. Both reset_token and new_password fields are required for this phase.

The password reset process enforces strict security: tokens are single-use and expire after 1 hour, passwords must be different from the current password, new passwords are hashed using bcrypt or Argon2 before storage, and all existing user sessions are terminated after successful password change.

ITodoAppAuthPasswordResetResponse.description:
Response body for password reset operations indicating the status and outcome of the operation.

For Phase 1 (Password Reset Initiation): Returns a generic confirmation message indicating password reset instructions have been sent to the user's email address. Does not reveal whether the email was found in the system (for security, to prevent email enumeration attacks).

For Phase 2 (Password Reset Completion): Returns a success confirmation indicating the password has been successfully reset. Instructs the user to log in with their new password. All existing sessions for that user have been automatically invalidated (expired_at timestamp set in todo_app_user_sessions records), so the user must re-authenticate.

The response includes appropriate HTTP status codes: 200 OK for successful operations, 400 Bad Request for validation errors (invalid email format, expired token, invalid new password), 404 Not Found for non-existent email (though frontend receives same generic message as 200 OK for security), and 500 Internal Server Error for unexpected server failures.

success.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the password reset operation completed successfully. true = operation succeeded, false = operation failed. Used by client to determine whether to show success or error messaging.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the outcome of the password reset operation.

For Phase 1 success: 'If an account exists with this email, password reset instructions have been sent. Please check your email.'

For Phase 2 success: 'Your password has been reset successfully. You can now log in with your new password.'

For Phase 1 validation error (invalid email format): 'Please enter a valid email address (e.g., user@example.com).'

For Phase 2 validation errors: 'Password must be at least 8 characters long' or 'Passwords do not match. Please re-enter your password.' or 'Your new password must be different from your current password.'

For expired/invalid token: 'Your password reset link has expired. Please request a new password reset.'

status_code.description:
Machine-readable status code for the password reset operation result.

Examples: 'PASSWORD_RESET_EMAIL_SENT' (Phase 1 success), 'PASSWORD_RESET_SUCCESS' (Phase 2 success), 'INVALID_INPUT_EMAIL_FORMAT' (invalid email), 'INVALID_INPUT_PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT' (password < 8 chars), 'PASSWORD_MISMATCH' (confirm_password doesn't match new_password), 'PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED' (token older than 1 hour), 'PASSWORD_RESET_INVALID_TOKEN' (token not found or already used), 'INVALID_INPUT_PASSWORD_SAME_AS_CURRENT' (new password same as old), 'USER_NOT_FOUND' (email not found, though frontend receives same message as success)

recovery_action.description:
Suggested action for the client/user in response to the operation result.

For Phase 1 success: 'check_email' - Instructs user to check their email for password reset instructions.

For Phase 2 success: 'redirect_to_login' - Instructs client to redirect user to login page so they can authenticate with new password.

For validation errors: 'retry_with_corrections' - User should correct the problematic fields and resubmit the form.

For expired token: 'try_reset_password' - User should click 'Forgot Password' again to request a new reset token.

For non-existent email: 'register_new_account' - Suggests user may need to create a new account if they don't have one.

For server errors: 'contact_support' - User should contact support with error code for assistance.

ITodoAppUser.IChangePassword.description: Request body for changing an authenticated user's password. User provides their current password for verification and a new password meeting security requirements (minimum 8 characters). The system validates the current password is correct and the new password is different from the old password. Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the user are invalidated and user must re-authenticate with the new password. This operation implements the password change workflow from requirement 02-user-actors-authentication.md section 'Account Security'.

current_password.description: User's current password in plaintext for verification. Required to ensure the user has authorization to change their password and prevent unauthorized password changes from compromised sessions. Must match the password hash stored in the database when compared using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. If incorrect, the operation is rejected with error 'Current password is incorrect'.

new_password.description: New password meeting security requirements. Must be at least 8 characters in length. Must differ from the current password - users cannot set a new password to the same value as their current password. The system rejects password changes if the new password matches the old password with error 'New password must be different from current password'. Backend will hash this plaintext password using bcrypt or Argon2 with unique salt before storing in database.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user whose password was changed. References the todo_app_users.id field. Confirms which user account was affected by the password change operation.

email.description: Email address of the user account. Confirms the account email associated with the password change. Identifies which user performed the password change.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating successful password change. Example: 'Password changed successfully. You will be logged out and must re-authenticate with your new password.'. Informs user of the success and that they need to log in again.

ITodoAppUser.IPasswordChanged.description: Response body confirming successful password change for an authenticated user. Returns the user ID and email to confirm which account's password was changed. Includes confirmation message explaining that all existing sessions have been invalidated and user must re-authenticate with their new password on next access. Implements the password change confirmation from requirement 02-user-actors-authentication.md section 'Account Security'.

ITodoAppUser.ISessionInfo.description:
Current authenticated user's active session information including session creation time, expiration time, and connection metadata. This DTO is returned by the session retrieval endpoint and provides users with details about their current login session, enabling them to verify they recognize the location, IP address, and device from which they are logged in. This supports security awareness by allowing users to detect potentially unauthorized sessions.

Session information includes complete details about when the session was established, when it will expire due to inactivity, and the connection context (IP address and referrer information) that led to the session creation. Users can use this information to verify the session originated from a recognized location and helps identify security issues if an unrecognized IP or location is shown.

userId.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user who owns this session. This ID links the session to the specific user account and is extracted from the JWT token to identify which user is currently logged in. The user ID remains constant for the entire lifetime of the session.

userEmail.description: Email address of the authenticated user. This is the email used to log in to the account and serves as the human-readable identifier for which user account this session belongs to. Helps users verify they recognize the email of the account they are logged into.

sessionId.description: Unique identifier for this specific session. Each login creates a new session with its own ID. Multiple concurrent sessions can exist for the same user (e.g., logged in from multiple devices), and each will have a distinct session ID. The session ID is used to track this particular login session independently.

createdAt.description: Timestamp in UTC when this session was established - i.e., when the user successfully authenticated and logged in. This timestamp marks the exact moment the user logged in and created this session. Users can check this timestamp to verify it matches when they logged in.

expiredAt.description: Timestamp in UTC when this session expires or was terminated. When NULL, the session is still active. When populated, indicates when the session ended (either due to inactivity timeout, explicit logout by user, or admin termination). Sessions automatically expire after 30 minutes of inactivity. Users can check this to understand when their current session will automatically expire.

ipAddress.description: IP address from which the user established this session. Displayed to user for security verification - users should recognize this IP address as originating from their device or network. If user sees an unfamiliar IP address, it may indicate unauthorized login from a different location. Example format: '192.168.1.100' or '2001:db8::1' for IPv6 addresses.

referrerUrl.description: HTTP referrer URL indicating the previous page or application that led to this session creation. Shows where the user was before logging in. This helps establish context about the user's access path and browser history that led to the login.

connectionUrl.description: The connection URL / request URL where the session was established. Captures the entry point where the user logged in and the path they were accessing when they authenticated. Helps users verify they logged in at a recognized application endpoint.

email.description: New email address for the user account. Must be unique across all users in the system - the system verifies the new email is not already in use by another account before allowing the change. Email must follow valid RFC 5322 format. Optional field - if not provided in the update request, the user's current email is unchanged. When changed, the user's login email changes immediately to the new email address.

oneOf.description: User can log in and access the system.
User cannot log in but account data is preserved.

status.description: New account status for the user. Valid values are 'active' (user can log in and access the system) or 'inactive' (user cannot log in but account data is preserved). Optional field - if not provided, status remains unchanged. When status is changed to 'inactive' by an admin, the user's active sessions are immediately terminated and they cannot log in until status is changed back to 'active'. Only admins can modify status of other users; regular users can only change their own email.

ITodoAppUser.IUpdate.description:
Request body DTO for updating an existing user account. This DTO defines which user account fields can be modified through the user update operation. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates where only specified fields are changed while unmodified fields retain their previous values.

Regular authenticated users can update only their own account using this DTO to modify their email address. System administrators can use this DTO to update any user account including email and account status for administrative purposes. Password changes are handled through a separate password reset flow and cannot be changed through this general update endpoint.

All input data is validated before being persisted: email addresses must be unique across the system and follow valid format; status values must be one of the allowed values ('active' or 'inactive'). The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated to the current time when any field is modified by the system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. System-generated and immutable. Never changes after creation.

todo_app_user_id.description: User identifier who owns this todo. Establishes the one-to-many relationship where each todo belongs to exactly one user. Set at creation time and never changes. Used for data isolation and access control to ensure only the owner can view, modify, or delete this todo.

title.description: Required todo title describing what needs to be done. Non-empty string with maximum 255 characters. Primary identifier for the todo from the user perspective. Cannot be empty or contain only whitespace.

description.description: Optional detailed information and context about the todo. Additional notes and instructions beyond the title. Maximum 2000 characters. Can be null or empty if user does not provide additional details. Stored as null in database when not provided.

oneOf.description: Incomplete todo requiring action.
Finished todo.

status.description: Current state of the todo representing whether the task is incomplete or finished. Valid values: 'active' for incomplete todos requiring action, 'completed' for finished todos. Defaults to 'active' when todo is created. Determines visibility in active versus completed todo lists.

oneOf.description: Non-urgent task.
Standard priority task.
Urgent task.

priority.description: Optional importance level of the todo helping users prioritize their work. Valid values: 'low' for non-urgent tasks, 'medium' for standard priority, 'high' for urgent tasks. Defaults to 'medium' if not specified by user. This field always has a value in responses because the system defaults to 'medium' if not explicitly set. Helps users understand which tasks should be done first.

due_date.description: Optional target completion date for the todo in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must not be in the past. Helps users manage deadlines and organize work by urgency. Can be null when no specific deadline exists. Example: '2025-12-31'.

created_at.description: System-generated timestamp in UTC when the todo was created. Immutable after creation, never changes throughout the todo's lifetime. Records exactly when the user captured the task. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

updated_at.description: System-generated timestamp in UTC of the most recent modification to any property of the todo. Automatically updated every time any field changes (title, description, status, priority, due date). Enables tracking recent activity and sorting todos by recency. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

completed_at.description: System-generated timestamp in UTC when the todo was marked as completed. Only populated when status is 'completed'. Automatically cleared when status changes back to 'active' from completed. Null for active todos. Records exactly when the user finished the task.

ITodoAppTodo.description: Core todo item entity representing a single task managed by a user. Each todo belongs exclusively to one user and tracks the complete lifecycle from creation through completion. Contains required properties (title, status) and optional properties (description, priority, due_date). Timestamps track creation, modification, and completion events. This is the central business object enabling users to capture, organize, and track their work. All optional fields (description, due_date, completed_at) are expressed using oneOf with null type to maintain consistency in schema representation.

title.description: Required todo title describing what needs to be done. Non-empty string with maximum 255 characters. Cannot be empty or contain only whitespace. Matches todo_app_todos.title field from Prisma schema which stores the primary description of what the user needs to accomplish.

description.description: Optional detailed information and context about the todo. Additional notes beyond the title. Maximum 2000 characters. Can be omitted if user does not provide additional details. Matches todo_app_todos.description field which can be null if not provided.

priority.description: Optional importance level of the todo helping users prioritize work. Valid values: 'low', 'medium', 'high'. Defaults to 'medium' if not specified by the user. Matches todo_app_todos.priority field. Helps users understand task urgency and organize work by importance.

due_date.description: Optional target completion date in ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Must not be in the past. Helps users manage deadlines. Can be omitted when no specific deadline exists. Matches todo_app_todos.due_date field which can be null. Example: '2025-12-31'. Validation: cannot be earlier than today's date.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description: Request body schema for creating a new todo item. The user provides a required title (maximum 255 characters) and may optionally provide description (max 2000 characters), priority level ('low'/'medium'/'high', defaults to 'medium'), and future due date (ISO 8601 format). The system automatically assigns todo ID (UUID), sets status to 'active', records creation and updated timestamps in UTC, associates the todo exclusively with the authenticated user (todo_app_user_id), and stores all data in todo_app_todos table.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Starts at 1 for the first page. Used for offset-based pagination to handle large todo lists efficiently. Default is page 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Number of todo items to return per page for pagination. Controls page size. Default is 20 items per page. Maximum allowed is 100 items per page to prevent memory issues and ensure query performance under 2 seconds.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the todo list by. Valid values: 'created_at' (newest first by default), 'due_date' (earliest deadlines first), 'priority' (high priority first), 'status' (active first), 'updated_at' (recently modified first). Defaults to 'created_at' if not specified. Corresponds to todo_app_todos table fields.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction for the selected sort field. Valid values: 'asc' for ascending order, 'desc' for descending order. Defaults to 'desc' (newest/highest first) if not specified.

status.description: Filter todos by status - show only active (incomplete) or completed todos. If not specified, returns todos with all statuses. Corresponds to todo_app_todos.status field ('active' or 'completed' values).

priority.description: Filter todos by priority level. If specified, returns only todos with matching priority. Can be 'low', 'medium', or 'high'. If not specified, returns todos with all priority levels. Corresponds to todo_app_todos.priority field.

due_date_from.description: Filter todos by due date range - start date (inclusive) in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). When specified along with due_date_to, returns todos with due dates within this range. If only due_date_from is specified, returns todos with due dates on or after this date. Filters against todo_app_todos.due_date field.

due_date_to.description: Filter todos by due date range - end date (inclusive) in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). When specified along with due_date_from, returns todos with due dates within this range. If only due_date_to is specified, returns todos with due dates on or before this date. Filters against todo_app_todos.due_date field.

title_search.description: Full-text search term to find todos by matching in title field. Uses text matching against todo_app_todos.title field. Partial matches supported. Case-insensitive. Uses GIN trigram index for performance. Useful for quickly finding specific todos by searching their titles.

description_search.description: Full-text search term to find todos by matching in description field. Uses text matching against todo_app_todos.description field. Partial matches supported. Case-insensitive. Uses GIN trigram index for performance. Useful for finding todos by keywords in their detailed descriptions.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description: Query parameters for filtering, searching, sorting, and paginating the todo list. Allows users to retrieve their todos with advanced filtering and organization options. Supports filtering by status (active/completed), priority level (low/medium/high), due date range, and searching by text in title and description. Results can be sorted by multiple fields and paginated. All parameters are optional - if not specified, sensible defaults are used (first page, 20 items per page, sorted by created_at descending, all statuses and priorities shown). Queries filter automatically by authenticated user's todo_app_user_id for data isolation.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item for use in list views, embedded references, and lightweight responses.

This summary type provides core todo information essential for displaying tasks in list contexts without including extensive details. It is used when returning lists of todos, showing todo references in other contexts, or providing quick views of work status.

The summary includes the todo's unique identifier, title for quick recognition, status and priority for understanding task state and importance, due date if provided for deadline awareness, creation timestamp for sorting and audit, and completion timestamp when the todo is finished. This information enables users to see their work at a glance and understand task status, priority, and deadlines without loading full todo details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this todo and never changes after creation.

overdue_todos_count.description: Number of active (incomplete) todos that have due dates in the past (before today). Highlights todos that the user should have completed already, drawing attention to tasks requiring immediate attention.

upcoming_todos_count.description: Number of active todos with due dates in the future (after today). Provides visibility into upcoming deadlines the user is planning for. Helps users understand their forward-looking workload.

ITodoAppDashboard.description: Dashboard overview object containing aggregated todo statistics and activity summary for the authenticated user. This object provides the authenticated user with a comprehensive snapshot of their todo management activity and productivity metrics on a single dashboard view. The dashboard displays immediate insights about current workload, recent activity, completion progress, and upcoming deadlines. The dashboard aggregates data from the todo_app_todos table filtered for the authenticated user (matching todo_app_user_id), computing statistics by status, completion dates, priority levels, and due dates. All calculations reflect only the authenticated user's todos, enforcing strict data isolation. Dashboard metrics are calculated fresh on each request to ensure current accuracy. The dashboard typically loads within 2 seconds even for users with large numbers of todos (up to 10,000 items), through optimized database queries and potential caching strategies. The dashboard serves as the primary user interface post-authentication, enabling users to quickly assess their productivity, understand their current workload, celebrate recent accomplishments, and identify urgent items requiring immediate attention.

ITodoAppTodoDashboardSummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a todo item as displayed in the user's dashboard.

This summary includes essential todo information needed for dashboard display and quick action, including the todo's identity (id, todo owner id, title), current state (status, priority), detailed context (description), timing information (due date, created/completed timestamps).

The summary is optimized for display in lists (recently added todos, recently completed todos) on the dashboard, providing enough detail for users to understand and interact with their todos without full verbose information.

This summary type is derived from todo_app_todos table records, selecting key fields relevant to dashboard presentation filtered by authenticated user's todo_app_user_id for data isolation. Optional fields (description, due_date, completed_at) may be null and are not required in all cases - they are populated only when relevant to the todo's state.

total_users_count.description: Total number of user accounts registered in the system. Counts all records in todo_app_users table regardless of account status (active, inactive, or deleted). Represents the total user base size across all time.

active_users_count.description: Number of user accounts currently in 'active' status and NOT deleted. Calculated by filtering todo_app_users where status = 'active' and deleted_at IS NULL. Represents the active user population available to use the system.

inactive_users_count.description: Number of user accounts marked as deleted (soft deleted). Calculated by filtering todo_app_users where deleted_at IS NOT NULL. Represents users who have been removed from active system access. Does not include suspended accounts with inactive status but null deleted_at.

new_users_today_count.description: Number of new user accounts created today. Calculated by counting todo_app_users records where DATE(created_at) = TODAY(). Shows new user registration activity for the current calendar day. Enables admins to monitor daily onboarding rate.

new_users_this_week_count.description: Number of new user accounts created during the current calendar week (Monday through today). Calculated by filtering todo_app_users where created_at falls within the current week date range. Indicates weekly user growth rate for trend analysis.

new_users_this_month_count.description: Number of new user accounts created during the current calendar month. Calculated by filtering todo_app_users where MONTH(created_at) = CURRENT_MONTH() and YEAR(created_at) = CURRENT_YEAR(). Indicates monthly user growth rate for capacity planning.

total_todos_count.description: Total number of todos created across all users in the system since application started. Counts all records in todo_app_todos table. Represents the total work items ever captured and managed in the system. Metric for application usage volume.

active_todos_count.description: Number of incomplete todos across all users (status = 'active'). Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where status = 'active'. Represents the current system workload and pending work needing attention. Shows urgency and work backlog.

completed_todos_count.description: Number of completed todos across all users (status = 'completed'). Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where status = 'completed'. Shows the volume of completed work and productivity over system lifetime. Indicates total accomplished work.

completion_rate_percentage.description: Overall system completion rate as a percentage. Calculated as (completed_todos_count / total_todos_count * 100) when total_todos_count > 0; returns 0 when total_todos_count = 0 (no division by zero). Ranges from 0 to 100. Indicates overall system productivity trend and user success rate in finishing captured tasks.

average_todos_per_user.description: Average number of todos created per user. Calculated as total_todos_count / active_users_count when active_users_count > 0; returns 0 when active_users_count = 0 (no division by zero). Shows typical user engagement level and workload patterns. Helps identify if users are actively using the system for task capture.

todos_completed_today_count.description: Number of todos marked as completed today across all users. Calculated by counting todo_app_todos records where DATE(completed_at) = TODAY(). Shows daily completion activity and same-day task completion rate. Indicates team productivity for the current day.

todos_completed_this_week_count.description: Number of todos marked as completed during the current calendar week across all users. Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where completed_at falls within current week date range. Indicates weekly completion volume and sustained productivity trend for 7-day period.

todos_completed_this_month_count.description: Number of todos marked as completed during the current calendar month across all users. Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where MONTH(completed_at) = CURRENT_MONTH() and YEAR(completed_at) = CURRENT_YEAR(). Indicates monthly completion trends for longer-term capacity and performance analysis.

overdue_todos_count.description: Number of active todos across all users that have due dates in the past (before today). Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where status = 'active' and due_date < TODAY(). Identifies system-wide overdue work requiring immediate attention. Shows tasks past their deadline still pending completion.

high_priority_todos_count.description: Number of active todos across all users with priority level set to 'high'. Calculated by filtering todo_app_todos where status = 'active' and priority = 'high'. Shows the volume of urgent work in the system. Indicates critical tasks needing immediate focus.

most_active_users.description: Array of the most active users by todo creation/completion volume. Typically the top 5-10 users ranked by total todos created. Includes user_id, email, todos_created_count, todos_completed_count, and user_completion_rate_percentage for each active user. Enables administrators to identify highly engaged users and power users of the system. Referenced schema ITodoAppStatisticsActiveUser contains detailed user engagement metrics.

ITodoAppStatistics.description:
System-wide statistics object containing aggregated metrics about users, todos, activity patterns, and system health.

This object provides administrators with comprehensive system-level insights enabling monitoring of application usage, user engagement, productivity trends, and system capacity planning. The statistics aggregate data from todo_app_users and todo_app_todos tables across all users in the system.

The statistics include user metrics (total registered, active, new registrations by timeframe), todo metrics (total created, active, completed, completion rates), activity trends (completions by timeframe, overdue items, high-priority work), and engagement metrics (average todos per user, most active users).

These statistics serve administrative purposes including system monitoring, usage reporting for stakeholders, capacity planning decisions, feature prioritization based on usage patterns, and trend analysis for understanding application adoption and engagement over time.

Statistics are restricted to authenticated users with admin role. Access is enforced through JWT token role verification - system checks user's 'admin' role claim in JWT token before returning statistics. Regular users attempting to access receive HTTP 403 Forbidden with message 'Access denied. This operation is restricted to administrators.' When an admin accesses statistics, the access is logged in todo_app_audit_logs table with action_type 'admin_statistics_access' for audit trail and compliance purposes.

The statistics calculations include defensive coding for division by zero (percentage and average calculations return 0 when denominators are zero). Statistics calculations aggregate across all system data and support optional date range filtering to enable historical trend analysis and comparison of metrics over different time periods. The operation returns fresh calculations on each request to ensure accuracy.

user_id.description: Unique identifier of the active user. Matches todo_app_users.id. Used to reference the specific user for admin operations or detailed analysis.

email.description: Email address of the active user. Matches todo_app_users.email. Provides way to identify the user by their login credential.

todos_created_count.description: Total number of todos created by this user. Calculated by counting todo_app_todos records where todo_app_user_id matches the user. Indicates the user's engagement level and activity volume.

todos_completed_count.description: Total number of todos marked as completed by this user. Calculated by counting todo_app_todos records where todo_app_user_id matches the user and status = 'completed'. Indicates user's productivity and task completion rate.

user_completion_rate_percentage.description: This user's personal completion rate as a percentage. Calculated as (todos_completed_count / todos_created_count * 100) when todos_completed_count > 0. Ranges from 0 to 100. Indicates the user's individual productivity level.

ITodoAppStatisticsActiveUser.description:
Summary information about an active user included in system-wide statistics, showing their engagement and productivity metrics.

This summary captures key metrics about individual users for administrators to identify highly engaged users, power users of the system, and engagement patterns. The summary includes the user's identity (user_id, email), activity metrics (todos created, todos completed), and performance metrics (individual completion rate).

These active user summaries are used in the ITodoAppStatistics most_active_users array to highlight the most engaged users in the system, enabling administrators to understand engagement patterns and identify power users driving adoption.

Data is derived from todo_app_users and todo_app_todos tables, aggregating todos created and completed for each user.

ITodoAppAuditLog.description:
Immutable audit trail record documenting a single administrative action performed by an admin user.

Each audit log entry captures what admin performed what action, on what resource, when, and from where. This entity implements the audit logging requirements from 07-admin-features.md section 5.2.

The audit trail is append-only - entries are never modified or deleted after creation. Used for security monitoring, compliance reporting, investigating security incidents, and tracking admin accountability. Every administrative operation that affects user accounts or system state generates an audit log entry.

Audit logs are essential for compliance, enabling forensic analysis of security incidents, and maintaining accountability for all administrative actions. Access to audit logs is restricted to authorized administrators only.

ITodoAppActivityLog.description:

Each activity log entry captures what user performed what action, what resource was affected, when, and from where. This entity tracks all critical user actions including todo creation, updates, deletions, completion tracking, and authentication events.

Activity logs are append-only records maintained for audit trail, user tracking, and system monitoring purposes. Used for detecting unusual user patterns, investigating user-reported issues, and understanding user engagement with the application.

ITodoAppBackup.description:
System backup snapshot metadata and status information. Represents a point-in-time backup of the entire application database and user data.

Each backup captures the complete state of all system data at a specific moment in time, including all user accounts, todos, sessions, and audit logs. Backups are automatically encrypted and stored separately from production systems for disaster recovery and data protection purposes.

Administrators use backup information to monitor backup coverage, verify backup integrity, and identify available backups for data restoration. Backup records include creation timestamp, size, verification status, and completion state.

id.description: Unique identifier for this backup snapshot. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies the backup record across all backups in the system.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the backup was initiated. Indicates the point-in-time that this backup captures. Stored in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00Z).

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the backup completed successfully. NULL if backup is still in progress or failed. Indicates when the backup snapshot was fully captured and ready for use.

size_bytes.description: Size of the backup in bytes. Indicates the storage space required for this backup snapshot. Helps administrators understand backup storage requirements and trends.

is_verified.description: Whether this backup has been verified as valid and restorable. TRUE indicates the backup integrity has been tested and the backup can be used for data restoration. FALSE means verification is pending or verification failed.

status.description:
Current status of the backup operation. Valid values: 'pending' (backup not yet started), 'in_progress' (backup currently running), 'completed' (backup finished successfully), 'failed' (backup operation encountered an error).

Status indicates the current state of the backup process and helps administrators understand whether the backup is ready for use or still being prepared.

ITodoAppBackup.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a system backup for list displays. Contains essential backup information for administrators to quickly understand backup coverage and availability.

This summary format is used when displaying lists of multiple backups to administrators. It provides the most important backup metadata (creation time, status, size, verification state) without excessive detail, enabling efficient browsing of available backup snapshots.

id.description: Unique identifier for this backup snapshot. System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies the backup record for reference and retrieval.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the backup was initiated. Indicates the point-in-time that this backup captures. Stored in ISO 8601 format with UTC timezone (e.g., 2024-01-15T14:30:00Z).

size_bytes.description: Size of the backup in bytes. Provides administrators with understanding of backup storage requirements and helps track storage usage trends.

is_verified.description: Whether this backup has been verified as valid and restorable. Indicates whether the backup integrity has been tested and the backup is safe to use for data restoration.

status.description: Current status of the backup operation. Values: 'pending', 'in_progress', 'completed', 'failed'. Provides quick indication of whether backup is ready for use or still in progress.

confirmation_phrase.description:
Admin's explicit confirmation phrase to verify they understand the destructive nature of backup restoration. Must match the expected confirmation phrase (typically 'CONFIRM') to proceed with restoration. This prevents accidental data loss due to misclicked buttons.

The admin must type this exact phrase in the confirmation dialog, demonstrating they have read and understood the warning about data loss. Any changes made to the application after the backup timestamp will be permanently lost and replaced with the backed-up versions.

reason.description:
Admin's explanation of why this backup restoration is necessary. Used for audit trail documentation and compliance purposes. Examples: 'Data corruption detected in production', 'Recovering from ransomware attack', 'Rolling back erroneous configuration change'.

This reason is recorded in the admin audit trail along with the restoration action for future reference and accountability.

ITodoAppAdminBackup.IRestore.description:
Request body for backup restoration operation. Contains the confirmation from the admin that they understand the consequences of restoration (all current data will be overwritten) and the reason for performing this sensitive operation.

Restoration is a destructive operation that will overwrite all current application data with the backed-up version, rolling back any changes made after the backup was created. The confirmation phrase requirement ensures the admin has explicitly confirmed they understand this consequence.

The reason field provides audit trail documentation of why the restoration was performed, supporting compliance requirements and future incident investigations.

success.description: Boolean indicating whether the backup restoration operation completed successfully. True means the backup has been fully restored and the system is now running with the backed-up state. False indicates the restoration failed partway through, though the system attempts to ensure atomicity so partial restores do not occur.

backup_id.description: Unique identifier of the backup that was restored. References the backup snapshot used for this restoration operation. Enables auditing which backup version was restored.

restored_timestamp.description: Timestamp in UTC ISO 8601 format indicating the point-in-time state that the system has been restored to. This is the created_at timestamp from the selected backup. All application data now reflects the state as it existed at this timestamp.

restoration_completed_at.description: Timestamp in UTC ISO 8601 format when the restoration operation completed. Indicates when the system finished writing the backed-up data to the production database and became available with the restored state.

users_restored.description: Number of user accounts included in the restoration. Indicates how many user records were restored from the backup. Users will need to log in again after restoration completes.

todos_restored.description: Number of todo items included in the restoration. Indicates how many task items were restored from the backup. Todos will revert to their state at the backup timestamp.

message.description:
Human-readable message describing the restoration result. Examples: 'Backup restoration completed successfully. System restored to 2024-10-31 14:00:00 UTC. All users have been logged out and must log in again.' or 'Backup restoration completed with warnings. Some audit logs could not be fully restored.'.

Provides additional context about the restoration operation and any notable conditions or side effects.

ITodoAppAdminBackup.IRestoreResult.description:
Response body confirming successful backup restoration with detailed information about what was restored. Indicates that the Todo application has been restored to the point-in-time state captured in the backup.

The restoration operation has completed and all data (users, todos, audit logs) have been written to the production database. The system is now operating with the backed-up state. All users will see the application as it existed at the restored_timestamp.

Users will need to log in again after the restoration, as all sessions are invalidated during the restoration process. The restoration action is logged in the admin audit trail with full details for compliance and security purposes.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a user account for use in list views, references, and lightweight responses.

This summary type provides essential user identification information without exposing sensitive account details. It is used when user information is needed as context (e.g., displaying the owner of a todo) or when returning lists of users in administrative interfaces.

The summary includes the user's unique identifier, email address for communication, account status to indicate if the user can access the system, and account creation timestamp for audit purposes. This information is sufficient for most use cases while maintaining data minimalism and security boundaries.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user. System-generated UUID that never changes after account creation and uniquely identifies this user across the entire system.

email.description: User's email address used as the unique login identifier for authentication. Must follow valid email format (RFC 5322). Unique across all user accounts in the system.

oneOf.description: User account is active and can access the system
User account is inactive and cannot access the system

status.description: Current account status indicating whether the user can access the system. Valid values are 'active' (user can log in and manage todos) or 'inactive' (user cannot log in, data preserved). Determines login eligibility.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the user registered and created their account. Automatically set by system at account creation time and never changes after creation. Records when user joined the service.

ITodoAppSession.description:
User authentication session representing an active login connection. Records when a user successfully authenticates and maintains session state across multiple requests. Each session is associated with a specific user and tracks connection metadata (IP address, entry point URL, referrer). Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or explicit logout, requiring user to re-authenticate.

Session records are immutable after creation and used for security tracking, audit trail purposes, and enabling multi-device concurrent sessions for the same user.

id.description: Unique session identifier (UUID). System-generated primary key for this session record. Used to reference and track the specific authenticated session throughout its lifetime.

todo_app_user_id.description: Foreign key reference to the authenticated user (todo_app_users.id). Establishes which user this session belongs to. Each session is associated with exactly one user account. Multiple concurrent sessions are allowed per user across different devices.

ip.description: Client IP address from which this session was established. Captured when user successfully authenticates. Used for security monitoring, tracking login locations from different networks, and audit trail purposes. Example: '192.168.1.100' or '2001:db8::1'.

href.description: Connection URL / request URL when this session was established. Captures the entry point that initiated the session creation. Represents the application URL or page where the user logged in.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page or application that led to this session creation. Tracks the source of the user's navigation to the login page. Used for understanding user journey and traffic sources.

created_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the session was established after successful user authentication. Automatically set by the system when user logs in. Recorded in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Used for session age tracking and timeout calculations.

expired_at.description: Timestamp in UTC when the session expires or was explicitly terminated by user logout. NULL (null value) indicates the session is currently active and not expired. When populated, indicates user must re-authenticate. Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity or explicit logout. Stored in ISO 8601 format.
